examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Inverse Laplace Transform of a Function Using the Scalar Multiplication Property
examples.worked_solution:
From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{9t}} & =\frac{1}{s-9},\,s>9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by applying the inverse Laplace transform to the above result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{9t}} & =\frac{1}{s-9} \\ {L}^{-1}{L{{e}^{9t}}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-9}} \\ {e}^{9t} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-9}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-9}} & ={e}^{9t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplicative property of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}7\cdot {L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-9}}=7\cdot {e}^{9t} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{7}{s-9}}=7{e}^{9t}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
We decompose the fraction into a sum of partial fractions, as follows:

$$
\frac{2s+15}{{s}^{2}+9}=\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+9}+\frac{15}{{s}^{2}+9}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0 \\ L{\operatorname{sin}⁡3t} & =\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition and multiplication properties of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+9}+\frac{15}{{s}^{2}+9}} & =2{L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9}}+5{L}^{-1}{\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+9}} \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+5\operatorname{sin}⁡3t.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{2s+15}{{s}^{2}+9}$ is $f(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+5\operatorname{sin}⁡3t.$
